facts.fact: Gabonactu reports that a joint visit by the project's technical committee (COTECH) and the World Bank on 23 October 2025 found the eGabon-SIS system in effective use at the Lalala and Glass health centres in Libreville, two of the 13 pilot sites chosen in Grand Libreville.

Two health centres, Lalala and Glass, were confirmed using the system on 23 October 2025, among 13 pilot sites in Grand Libreville, per Gabonactu; the document gives no count of primary clinics nationally and no denominator.

On 23 October 2025 the chief doctor of the Lalala health centre said a patient can now be found in different facilities under a unique identifier, and the World Bank's specialist said patients can retrieve at another hospital the information entered at the centre; the document does not say whether entry is made at the point of care.

Gabonactu states on 25 October 2025 that the project is implemented by the state digital agency ANINF and followed by a project technical committee (COTECH); no health ministry unit is named as owner.
Gabonactu states on 25 October 2025 that the eGabon-SIS project is financed by the World Bank; no domestic budget line is mentioned.

A joint COTECH and World Bank monitoring visit on 23 October 2025 found the system operating at two Libreville health centres, with the technical committee's chair reporting effective interconnection between Grand Libreville hospitals.

systems.owner: implemented by ANINF; technical committee COTECH; World Bank financing
systems.tiers: 13 pilot sites in Grand Libreville, the Lalala and Glass health centres among them

note: Classed emr on a thin description: the document calls it hospital management software that organises consultations and lets patient information entered at one facility be retrieved at another under a unique identifier; it never uses the words patient record. The value shared is recorded on two of its three tests, point-of-care entry being unstated. owner:ministry stands for a state agency (ANINF), not a health ministry unit. The parent may prefer to drop any of the three.
